findings.where: Environment Loading Strategy (src/env.ts), step 1 and Append format note
findings.problem: atlas-credentials.env stores all values double-quoted, including MONGODB_URI="mongodb+srv://...". The design describes the URI as a bare string and never acknowledges the quotes. dotenv strips surrounding quotes so the runtime outcome is correct, but the load-bearing behavior is unstated, and the append logic's raw-file read will see the quotes.
findings.fix: State that values are double-quoted, dotenv strips them so config.mongoUri is the unquoted string passed to new MongoClient() as-is, and that the raw-file read used for append-detection must not be confused with the dotenv-parsed process.env values.

findings.problem: stripMongoId is the function the entire 'returns the exact League shape' guarantee rests on, but it is given no signature. A non-generic or any-typed version compiles while defeating type safety or fails to type-check across TeamDoc/BowlerDoc.
findings.fix: Specify: function stripMongoId<T extends { _id?: ObjectId }>({ _id, ...rest }: T): Omit<T, '_id'> { return rest }, and note Omit<TeamDoc,'_id'> is structurally Team, etc., so League is satisfied without casts.

findings.problem: Design says the /reports route is 'inside the <Layout> route', but App.tsx has no <Layout> wrapper element - Layout is a layout route with <Outlet/>. The phrasing could lead an implementer to wrap ReportsPage in a literal <Layout>, double-nesting the shell. Placement relative to the path='*' catch-all is also unstated.
findings.fix: Reword to: add <Route path='/reports' element={<ReportsPage />} /> as a child of the existing <Route element={<Layout />}> layout route next to the other page routes; order relative to path='*' is irrelevant in react-router v6.

findings.problem: The main.tsx edit to mount the League provider is asserted but never shown, and the exported component name is never given (only the hook useLeague() and the vague 'LeagueProvider'/'the provider'). All seven consumers (six pages + Layout.tsx) must import these exact names.
findings.fix: Name the exports explicitly (LeagueProvider component, useLeague hook) and show the main.tsx edit nesting <LeagueProvider> inside <AuthProvider> around <App/>, so Layout (rendered inside App) is covered.

findings.problem: Validation omits rules for homeSeries, awaySeries, lanes, homeTeamId, awayTeamId, week, and the empty-array/zero-series case. Seed data has awaySeries: 0, single-element awayGames, and differing array lengths, so an implementer guessing 'non-empty arrays' or 'series equals sum of games' would reject valid rows.
findings.fix: Specify per field: week positive int; lanes non-empty string; home/awayTeamId non-empty strings; home/awayGames arrays of numbers >= 0 (may be empty); home/awaySeries numbers >= 0 (NOT required to equal sum of games); home/awayPoints numbers >= 0; differing array lengths allowed.

findings.problem: The snippet uses Collection<...>, Db, and GridFSBucket in return types but imports only ObjectId from mongodb; copied verbatim it does not compile.
findings.fix: Show the full import, e.g. import { ObjectId, GridFSBucket, type Collection, type Db } from 'mongodb'.

findings.where: API Client getReportUrl and Reports list anchor
findings.problem: The relative /api/reports/:id anchor href works in dev only via the Vite proxy and in prod via same-origin; an implementer might 'fix' it to an absolute localhost:4000 URL that breaks in production.
findings.fix: Add a sentence: the relative /api/reports/:id href is resolved by the Vite proxy in dev and same-origin server in prod; do not hardcode the backend host.

findings.problem: Removing bowling-league.auth only when bowling-league.token is absent leaves a stale old-scheme object whenever a new token exists; the gating reads as a deliberate guard but is unnecessary.
findings.fix: Remove the old key unconditionally on first load; the new scheme never reads it.
